guards: No line is published without an official source for the event's identity and for the form inputs used in the calculation.
Where a required input (starting pitcher, lineup, going, weather, injury) is unconfirmed, the line is withheld and the match is flagged rather than priced on an assumption.
Margins are stated per market so a reader can back out the desk's raw probability: raw = published probability / (1 + margin).
The mandate window is -250 to +10000 American. A line shorter than -250 is still published where the analysis supports it, but is labelled out-of-window.
Confidence bands follow the published implied probability: high 65.0-71.4% (which is -186 to -250 American), medium 55.0-64.9%, low below 55.0%.
Every price is originated by this desk. No bookmaker price is copied, and no OLBG tip count is treated as a probability.

volleyball.summary: Two-way match market with no draw. Each side is rated from sets and points won per set across the current league season and from head-to-head set differential; the rating gap is converted to a match probability with the standard logistic link, then adjusted for home court (worth 0.15 to 0.30 of a set) and, for set-score markets, expanded through a per-set binomial.

markets.method: Logistic on rating gap; per-set win rate estimated from season set differential, then converted to a best-of-five match probability by summing binomial terms for 3-0, 3-1 and 3-2.
markets.inputs: League sets won/lost, points per set, head-to-head set record, home/away split

markets.method: Binomial with per-set probability from the rating gap, split across the three winning scorelines; sets are treated as independent within 0.02 tolerance.
Sum of the match-winner scenarios that produce each total; the over/under line is derived from the resulting distribution, not from a market quote.

volleyball.example: A side rated 0.62 per set in a best-of-five wins 3-0 at 23.8%, 3-1 at 26.6% and 3-2 at 24.7%, so the match probability is 75.1%; after the 4% margin the published line is about -270, which is inside the window only if the band check passes.

tennis.summary: Two-way match market. Player strength comes from tour ranking points and recent win rate on the same surface, blended into an Elo-style rating; the rating gap becomes a match probability, then a per-set probability for set and total-games markets.

markets.method: Elo-style rating difference plus a surface term; converted with the logistic link and then adjusted for best-of-three versus best-of-five format.
markets.inputs: Ranking points, surface win rate over the last 52 weeks, head-to-head, retirement history

markets.method: Per-set probability from the same rating gap; match probability is the binomial sum over straight-set and three-set paths.
Expected games from the per-set win rate and the players' service hold rates, then a normal approximation around the resulting mean.
markets.inputs: Hold rate, break rate, per-set probability

tennis.example: A 120-point rating edge converts to 68.5% in a best-of-three; with the 3.5% margin the line is -231 and the published win chance is 69.9%.

basketball.summary: Two-way market including overtime. Team strength is a points-per-100-possession differential adjusted for schedule and opponent, converted to a projected margin, then to a win probability with a margin standard deviation of 11.5 points.

markets.method: Normal approximation: P(win) = Phi(projected margin / 11.5). Projected margin from net rating differential plus 2.2 points home court.
markets.inputs: Net rating, pace, rest days, confirmed availability of listed starters

markets.method: Same projected margin against the desk's own spread line, priced with the same normal approximation and a push band of 0.5 points.
Expected possessions multiplied by expected points per possession for both teams; the line is the sum, priced with a 14-point standard deviation.

basketball.example: A projected 6.4-point home margin gives Phi(6.4/11.5) = 71.1% home; the 4% margin pushes the published line to about -285 and the pick is flagged out-of-window.

ice-hockey.summary: Three-way regulation market and two-way market including overtime and shootout. Strength is goal differential per 60 minutes at even strength; regulation probabilities come from a Poisson goal model, and the draw is removed to price the two-way market.

markets.method: Poisson goal model for 60 minutes, then the regulation draw is split 55/45 toward the stronger side for overtime; the three outcomes are renormalised to two.
markets.inputs: Goals for/against per 60, save percentage, special teams, confirmed starting goaltender

markets.method: Poisson with expected goals for each side; the draw is the P(equal goals) term.
The same Poisson grid, summed over the margin cells that satisfy the handicap, including the empty-net effect of 0.25 goals.
Poisson total with the line at the desk's own expected-goal sum rounded to the nearest half.

ice-hockey.example: Expected goals 3.15 to 2.70 gives a 44.1% regulation home win, 24.6% draw and 31.3% away; splitting the draw 55/45 yields 57.6% home on the two-way market.

rugby-union.summary: Three-way market (win, draw, loss) with handicap and total points. Strength is points differential adjusted for opponent quality; the draw is modelled explicitly at about 2% to 4% depending on the expected margin.

markets.method: Normal approximation on projected margin with a 13.5-point standard deviation; the draw band is plus or minus 0.5 points, and home advantage is 3.0 points.
markets.inputs: Points for/against, strength of schedule, recent results, confirmed team sheet

markets.method: The same projected margin against the desk's handicap line, with a push band.
Sum of expected points for both sides, priced with a 12-point standard deviation.
markets.inputs: Tries and penalty counts per match, kick success

rugby-union.example: A projected 7-point home margin puts the home win at 69.6% and the draw at 2.9%; the away win takes the remaining 27.5%.

rugby-league.summary: Three-way and two-way markets with handicap and totals. League strength is points differential per match with a larger home edge than rugby union because of the six-again rule's tempo effect.

markets.method: Normal approximation on projected margin, 14.5-point standard deviation, 3.5 points home advantage, draw band of plus or minus 0.5 points.
markets.inputs: Points for/against per match, recent form, confirmed 17-man squad

markets.method: Projected margin against the desk's handicap line with a push band.
Sum of expected points with a 13-point standard deviation.

rugby-league.example: A projected 12-point margin gives roughly 79% for the favourite before the draw band is removed.

handball.summary: Three-way market in most European leagues and two-way in some cup formats. Strength is goals for and against per match; expected goals come from an attack-versus-defence product, and the win probabilities come from a Poisson grid.

markets.method: Independent Poisson on each side's expected goals; draw is the diagonal of the grid, home edge worth 1.2 goals.
markets.inputs: Goals for/against per match, home/away split, EHF coefficient

markets.method: The Poisson grid summed over margin cells satisfying the handicap.
Poisson total around the desk's expected-goal sum, line rounded to the nearest whole goal.

handball.example: Expected goals 30.5 to 27.0 gives a 54.9% home win, 12.1% draw and 33.0% away win.

cricket.summary: Two-way match market and, in Test cricket, a three-way market with the draw. T20 and ODI probabilities come from a scoring-rate model; Test probabilities are driven by first-innings run expectation and remaining time.

markets.method: Expected run-rate differential converted to a projected run margin, then to a win probability with a 22-run standard deviation for T20 and 34 for ODI.
markets.inputs: Runs per over for and against, powerplay and death-over splits, toss and confirmed XI

markets.method: First-innings expectation, follow-on risk and the forecast overs remaining produce win/draw/loss shares; the draw is not a residual but is modelled from time lost.
markets.inputs: Batting averages, bowling averages, venue history, weather forecast

markets.method: Sum of per-match expectations across the scheduled fixtures.

cricket.example: A projected 18-run edge in a T20 gives 66.9% for the stronger side before the toss adjustment.

snooker.summary: Two-way match market in a best-of format. Strength is a per-frame probability built from ranking, recent frame differential and head-to-head; the match probability is the binomial sum over the required frames.

markets.method: Per-frame probability from frame win rate and break-building; converted to best-of-N by summing binomial probabilities of reaching the target first.
markets.inputs: Ranking, frames won/lost this season, head-to-head frame record, format

markets.method: The same binomial distribution, summed over the frames handicap.
Distribution of the finishing frame count from the binomial.

snooker.example: A 0.58 per-frame edge in a best-of-nine gives 66.3% for the match, with the most likely scoreline 5-3.

darts.summary: Two-way match market in legs or sets. Strength is three-dart average and checkout percentage; legs are converted to a match probability through a per-leg binomial or a set-based equivalent.

markets.method: Per-leg probability from three-dart average and checkout rate, then a binomial through the format; set play multiplies the leg model by a set conversion of 0.92.
markets.inputs: Three-dart average over 12 months, checkout percentage, head-to-head

markets.method: The same binomial summed over the legs handicap.
Leg distribution and expected 180s from the scoring rate.

darts.example: A 0.60 per-leg edge in a best-of-19 legs match gives 71.3%, which sits at the very edge of the price window.

baseball.summary: Two-way moneyline and run line. Strength is a run-expectation model driven by the confirmed starting pitchers, the bullpen and the park; the win probability comes from a run-scoring simulation with a 4.3-run standard deviation.

markets.method: Expected runs for each side from starter ERA/FIP and bullpen quality, park factor and lineup handedness; converted to a win probability with a 4.3-run standard deviation.
markets.inputs: Confirmed starters, bullpen ERA, park factor, lineup

markets.method: The same run distribution summed over the margin cells, with the home team's ninth inning conditioned on the score.
The sum of expected runs, priced with a 4.3-run standard deviation.

baseball.example: Expected runs 4.6 to 4.0 gives a 57.5% home win with the stated spread; the line lands near -135.

gaelic-sports.summary: Two-way market in Gaelic football and hurling, plus handicap and total points. Strength is scoring difference per game adjusted for division and opponent; draws are possible but rare and are priced as a no-bet on the two-way market.

markets.method: Normal approximation on projected margin with a 9.5-point standard deviation for football and 11 for hurling; home advantage 2.5 points.
markets.inputs: Scoring difference per game, division, league and championship form, confirmed panel

markets.method: Projected margin against the desk's handicap line with a push band.
Sum of expected scores with a 10-point standard deviation.

gaelic-sports.example: A projected 5-point football margin gives 70.1% for the favourite, which is inside the window at about -215.

greyhounds.summary: Race outright market across the six to eight runners, plus forecast and place markets. Strength is early pace and recent sectional times adjusted for trap and going; probabilities are normalised across the field.

markets.method: Trap-adjusted sectional rating for each runner, converted to a softmax probability across the field and normalised to 100%.
markets.inputs: Recent sectional times, trap bias at the track, going, grade

markets.method: Harville approximation on the win probabilities for the place terms advertised by the track.
markets.inputs: Win probabilities, field size, place terms

markets.method: Harville pairwise and triple products from the win probabilities.

greyhounds.example: A runner at 26% raw becomes 22.7% after the 12% field margin, which is about +340 American.

golf.summary: Tournament outright and place markets. Strength is strokes-gained per round over the last 24 rounds adjusted for course fit; win probability is normalised across the field and place probability uses the Harville approximation.

markets.method: Strokes-gained rating converted to a per-round standard deviation of 2.6 strokes; win probability from a Plackett-Luce normalisation across the confirmed field.
markets.inputs: Strokes gained tee-to-green and putting, course fit, field strength, confirmed entry list

markets.method: Harville approximation across the field for the place terms.
Head-to-head difference in strokes-gained rating, priced with a 2.6-stroke-per-round standard deviation over four rounds.

golf.example: A field-leading 8% raw win share becomes 6.9% after the field margin, which is about +1350 American.

motor-racing.summary: Race outright, podium and head-to-head markets. Strength is a car-plus-driver rating derived from qualifying and race pace; win probability is normalised across the grid, with a reliability term from recent retirements.

markets.method: Pace rating from qualifying gaps, converted to a softmax across the grid and multiplied by a reliability factor (finishing rate over the last 20 starts).
markets.inputs: Qualifying gaps, race pace, reliability, grid penalties

markets.method: Sum of the top-three finishing permutations from the same normalised distribution.
Two-way conversion of the pace gap between the pair.

motor-racing.example: A 24% raw win share becomes 21.1% after the grid margin, which is about +375 American.

gaelic_hurling.summary: Hurling uses the Gaelic football engine with a wider margin standard deviation and a higher expected score.
